Line 121 uses `subprocess.run(["open", str(OUTPUT_DIR)])` to reveal the output folder in Finder — this is macOS-only and works correctly on a Mac Mini. On any other OS it would fail, but that's presumably intentional.

---

notebooklm-py is an unofficial Python API and agentic skill for Google NotebookLM, providing full programmatic access to NotebookLM's features—including capabilities the web UI doesn't expose—via Python, CLI, and AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw. The library enables programmatic automation of NotebookLM features including notebook management, source integration, AI querying, and studio artifact generation (podcasts, videos, quizzes, etc.).

**2. notebooklm-skill (PleasePrompto/notebooklm-skill)**

This skill enables Claude Code to communicate directly with your Google NotebookLM notebooks, allowing you to query your uploaded documents and get source-grounded, citation-backed answers from Gemini, with features including browser automation, library management, persistent authentication, and answers exclusively from your own knowledge base.

**3. Additional Notable Implementations:**

- notebooklm-skill (claude-world) bridges NotebookLM's research capabilities with Claude's content generation, following a Research → Synthesis → Content Creation → Publishing workflow.

- jacob-bd/notebooklm-mcp-cli connects AI assistants (Claude, Gemini, Cursor, etc.) to NotebookLM.

All of these projects enable you to integrate Google NotebookLM with Claude Code for automated research and document querying without manual copy-pasting between applications.

5	
6	# NotebookLM Automation
7	
8	Complete programmatic access to Google NotebookLM—including capabilities not exposed in the web UI. Create notebooks, add sources (URLs, YouTube, PDFs, audio, video, images), chat with content, generate all artifact types, and download results in multiple formats.
9	
10	## Installation
11	
12	**From PyPI (Recommended):**
13	```bash
14	pip install notebooklm-py
15	```
16	
17	**From GitHub (use latest release tag, NOT main branch):**
18	```bash
19	# Get the latest release tag (using curl)
20	LATEST_TAG=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/teng-lin/notebooklm-py/releases/latest | grep '"tag_name"' | cut -d'"' -f4)
21	pip install "git+https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py@${LATEST_TAG}"
22	```
23	
24	⚠️ **DO NOT install from main branch** (`pip install git+https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py`). The main branch may contain unreleased/unstable changes. Always use PyPI or a specific release tag, unless you are testing unreleased features.

27

29	- `npx skills add teng-lin/notebooklm-py` installs this skill from the GitHub repository into compatible agent skill directories.
30	- If you are already reading this file inside an agent skill directory, the skill is already installed. You only need the Python package and authentication below.

37	## Prerequisites
38	
39	**IMPORTANT:** Before using any command, you MUST authenticate:
40	
41	```bash
42	notebooklm login          # Opens browser for Google OAuth
43	notebooklm list           # Verify authentication works
44	```
45	
46	If commands fail with authentication errors, re-run `notebooklm login`.
47	
48	### CI/CD, Multiple Accounts, and Parallel Agents
49	
50	For automated environments, multiple accounts, or parallel agent workflows:
51	
52	| Variable | Purpose |
53	|----------|---------|
54	| `NOTEBOOKLM_HOME` | Custom config directory (default: `~/.notebooklm`) |
55	| `NOTEBOOKLM_PROFILE` | Active profile name (default: `default`) |
56	| `NOTEBOOKLM_AUTH_JSON` | Inline auth JSON - no file writes needed |
57	
58	**CI/CD setup:** Set `NOTEBOOKLM_AUTH_JSON` from a secret containing your `storage_state.json` contents.
59	
60	**Multiple accounts:** Use named profiles (`notebooklm profile create work`, then `notebooklm -p work login`). Alternatively, use different `NOTEBOOKLM_HOME` directories per account.
61	
62	**Parallel agents:** The CLI stores notebook context in a shared file (`~/.notebooklm/context.json`). Multiple concurrent agents using `notebooklm use` can overwrite each other's context.
63	
64	**Solutions for parallel workflows:**
65	1. **Always use explicit notebook ID** (recommended): Pass `-n <notebook_id>` (for `wait`/`download` commands) or `--notebook <notebook_id>` (for others) instead of relying on `use`
66	2. **Per-agent isolation via profiles:** `export NOTEBOOKLM_PROFILE=agent-$ID` (each profile gets its own context file)
67	3. **Per-agent isolation via home:** Set unique `NOTEBOOKLM_HOME` per agent: `export NOTEBOOKLM_HOME=/tmp/agent-$ID`
68	4. **Use full UUIDs:** Avoid partial IDs in automation (they can become ambiguous)
69	
70	## Agent Setup Verification
71	
72	Before starting workflows, verify the CLI is ready:
73	
74	1. `notebooklm status` → Should show "Authenticated as: email@..."
75	2. `notebooklm list --json` → Should return valid JSON (even if empty notebooks list)
76	3. If either fails → Run `notebooklm login`

87	- "Create flashcards for studying"
88	- "Generate a video explainer"

94	## Autonomy Rules
95	
96	**Run automatically (no confirmation):**
97	- `notebooklm status` - check context
98	- `notebooklm auth check` - diagnose auth issues
99	- `notebooklm list` - list notebooks
100	- `notebooklm source list` - list sources
101	- `notebooklm artifact list` - list artifacts
102	- `notebooklm language list` - list supported languages
103	- `notebooklm language get` - get current language
104	- `notebooklm language set` - set language (global setting)
105	- `notebooklm artifact wait` - wait for artifact completion (in subagent context)
106	- `notebooklm source wait` - wait for source processing (in subagent context)
107	- `notebooklm research status` - check research status
108	- `notebooklm research wait` - wait for research (in subagent context)
109	- `notebooklm use <id>` - set context (⚠️ SINGLE-AGENT ONLY - use `-n` flag in parallel workflows)
110	- `notebooklm create` - create notebook
111	- `notebooklm ask "..."` - chat queries (without `--save-as-note`)
112	- `notebooklm history` - display conversation history (read-only)
113	- `notebooklm source add` - add sources
114	- `notebooklm profile list` - list profiles
115	- `notebooklm profile create` - create profile
116	- `notebooklm profile switch` - switch active profile
117	- `notebooklm doctor` - check environment health
118	
119	**Ask before running:**
120	- `notebooklm delete` - destructive
121	- `notebooklm generate *` - long-running, may fail
122	- `notebooklm download *` - writes to filesystem
123	- `notebooklm artifact wait` - long-running (when in main conversation)
124	- `notebooklm source wait` - long-running (when in main conversation)
125	- `notebooklm research wait` - long-running (when in main conversation)
126	- `notebooklm ask "..." --save-as-note` - writes a note
127	- `notebooklm history --save` - writes a note

196	**Parallel safety:** Use explicit notebook IDs in parallel workflows. Commands supporting `-n` shorthand: `artifact wait`, `source wait`, `research wait/status`, `download *`. Download commands also support `-a/--artifact`. Other commands use `--notebook`. For chat, use `-c <conversation_id>` to target a specific conversation.
197	
198	**Partial IDs:** Use first 6+ characters of UUIDs. Must be unique prefix (fails if ambiguous). Works for ID-based commands such as `use`, `source delete`, and `wait`. For exact source-title deletion, use `source delete-by-title "Title"`. For automation, prefer full UUIDs to avoid ambiguity.

200	## Command Output Formats
201	
202	Commands with `--json` return structured data for parsing:
203	
204	**Create notebook:**
205	```
206	$ notebooklm create "Research" --json
207	{"id": "abc123de-...", "title": "Research"}
208	```
209	
210	**Add source:**
211	```
212	$ notebooklm source add "https://example.com" --json
213	{"source_id": "def456...", "title": "Example", "status": "processing"}
214	```
215	
216	**Generate artifact:**
217	```
218	$ notebooklm generate audio "Focus on key points" --json
219	{"task_id": "xyz789...", "status": "pending"}
220	```
221	
222	**Chat with references:**
223	```
224	$ notebooklm ask "What is X?" --json
225	{"answer": "X is... [1] [2]", "conversation_id": "...", "turn_number": 1, "is_follow_up": false, "references": [{"source_id": "abc123...", "citation_number": 1, "cited_text": "Relevant passage from source..."}, {"source_id": "def456...", "citation_number": 2, "cited_text": "Another passage..."}]}
226	```
227	
228	**Source fulltext (get indexed content):**
229	```
230	$ notebooklm source fulltext <source_id> --json
231	{"source_id": "...", "title": "...", "char_count": 12345, "content": "Full indexed text..."}
232	```
233	
234	**Understanding citations:** The `cited_text` in references is often a snippet or section header, not the full quoted passage. The `start_char`/`end_char` positions reference NotebookLM's internal chunked index, not the raw fulltext. Use `SourceFulltext.find_citation_context()` to locate citations:
235	```python
236	fulltext = await client.sources.get_fulltext(notebook_id, ref.source_id)
237	matches = fulltext.find_citation_context(ref.cited_text)  # Returns list[(context, position)]
238	if matches:
239	    context, pos = matches[0]  # First match; check len(matches) > 1 for duplicates
240	```
241	
242	**Extract IDs:** Parse the `id`, `source_id`, or `task_id` field from JSON output.
243	
244	## Generation Types
245	
246	All generate commands support:
247	- `-s, --source` to use specific source(s) instead of all sources
248	- `--language` to set output language (defaults to configured language or 'en')
249	- `--json` for machine-readable output (returns `task_id` and `status`)
250	- `--retry N` to automatically retry on rate limits with exponential backoff
251	
252	| Type | Command | Options | Download |
253	|------|---------|---------|----------|
254	| Podcast | `generate audio` | `--format [deep-dive\|brief\|critique\|debate]`, `--length [short\|default\|long]` | .mp3 |
255	| Video | `generate video` | `--format [explainer\|brief]`, `--style [auto\|classic\|whiteboard\|kawaii\|anime\|watercolor\|retro-print\|heritage\|paper-craft]` | .mp4 |
256	| Slide Deck | `generate slide-deck` | `--format [detailed\|presenter]`, `--length [default\|short]` | .pdf / .pptx |
257	| Slide Revision | `generate revise-slide "prompt" --artifact <id> --slide N` | `--wait`, `--notebook` | *(re-downloads parent deck)* |
258	| Infographic | `generate infographic` | `--orientation [landscape\|portrait\|square]`, `--detail [concise\|standard\|detailed]`, `--style [auto\|sketch-note\|professional\|bento-grid\|editorial\|instructional\|bricks\|clay\|anime\|kawaii\|scientific]` | .png |
259	| Report | `generate report` | `--format [briefing-doc\|study-guide\|blog-post\|custom]`, `--append "extra instructions"` | .md |
260	| Mind Map | `generate mind-map` | *(sync, instant)* | .json |
261	| Data Table | `generate data-table` | description required | .csv |
262	| Quiz | `generate quiz` | `--difficulty [easy\|medium\|hard]`, `--quantity [fewer\|standard\|more]` | .json/.md/.html |
263	| Flashcards | `generate flashcards` | `--difficulty [easy\|medium\|hard]`, `--quantity [fewer\|standard\|more]` | .json/.md/.html |
264	
265	## Features Beyond the Web UI
266	
267	These capabilities are available via CLI but not in NotebookLM's web interface:
268	
269	| Feature | Command | Description |
270	|---------|---------|-------------|
271	| **Batch downloads** | `download <type> --all` | Download all artifacts of a type at once |
272	| **Quiz/Flashcard export** | `download quiz --format json` | Export as JSON, Markdown, or HTML (web UI only shows interactive view) |
273	| **Mind map extraction** | `download mind-map` | Export hierarchical JSON for visualization tools |
274	| **Data table export** | `download data-table` | Download structured tables as CSV |
275	| **Slide deck as PPTX** | `download slide-deck --format pptx` | Download slide deck as editable .pptx (web UI only offers PDF) |
276	| **Slide revision** | `generate revise-slide "prompt" --artifact <id> --slide N` | Modify individual slides with a natural-language prompt |
277	| **Report template append** | `generate report --format study-guide --append "..."` | Append custom instructions to built-in format templates without losing the format type |
278	| **Source fulltext** | `source fulltext <id>` | Retrieve the indexed text content of any source |
279	| **Save chat to note** | `ask "..." --save-as-note` / `history --save` | Save Q&A answers or conversation history as notebook notes |
280	| **Programmatic sharing** | `share` commands | Manage sharing permissions without the UI |
281	
282	## Common Workflows
283	
284	### Research to Podcast (Interactive)
285	**Time:** 5-10 minutes total
286	
287	1. `notebooklm create "Research: [topic]"` — *if fails: check auth with `notebooklm login`*
288	2. `notebooklm source add` for each URL/document — *if one fails: log warning, continue with others*
289	3. Wait for sources: `notebooklm source list --json` until all status=READY — *required before generation*
290	4. `notebooklm generate audio "Focus on [specific angle]"` (confirm when asked) — *if rate limited: wait 5 min, retry once*
291	5. Note the artifact ID returned
292	6. Check `notebooklm artifact list` later for status
293	7. `notebooklm download audio ./podcast.mp3` when complete (confirm when asked)
294	
295	### Research to Podcast (Automated with Subagent)
296	**Time:** 5-10 minutes, but continues in background
297	
298	When user wants full automation (generate and download when ready):
299	
300	1. Create notebook and add sources as usual
301	2. Wait for sources to be ready (use `source wait` or check `source list --json`)
302	3. Run `notebooklm generate audio "..." --json` → parse `artifact_id` from output
303	4. **Spawn a background agent** using Task tool:
304	   ```
305	   Task(
306	     prompt="Wait for artifact {artifact_id} in notebook {notebook_id} to complete, then download.
307	             Use: notebooklm artifact wait {artifact_id} -n {notebook_id} --timeout 600
308	             Then: notebooklm download audio ./podcast.mp3 -a {artifact_id} -n {notebook_id}",
309	     subagent_type="general-purpose"
310	   )
311	   ```
312	5. Main conversation continues while agent waits
313	
314	**Error handling in subagent:**
315	- If `artifact wait` returns exit code 2 (timeout): Report timeout, suggest checking `artifact list`
316	- If download fails: Check if artifact status is COMPLETED first
317	
318	**Benefits:** Non-blocking, user can do other work, automatic download on completion
319	
320	### Document Analysis
321	**Time:** 1-2 minutes
322	
323	1. `notebooklm create "Analysis: [project]"`
324	2. `notebooklm source add ./doc.pdf` (or URLs)
325	3. `notebooklm ask "Summarize the key points"`
326	4. `notebooklm ask "What are the main arguments?"`
327	5. Continue chatting as needed
328	
329	### Bulk Import
330	**Time:** Varies by source count
331	
332	1. `notebooklm create "Collection: [name]"`
333	2. Add multiple sources:
334	   ```bash
335	   notebooklm source add "https://url1.com"
336	   notebooklm source add "https://url2.com"
337	   notebooklm source add ./local-file.pdf
338	   ```
339	3. `notebooklm source list` to verify
340	
341	**Source limits:** Varies by plan—Standard: 50, Plus: 100, Pro: 300, Ultra: 600 sources per notebook. See [NotebookLM plans](https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16213268) for details. The CLI does not enforce these limits; they are applied by your NotebookLM account.
342	**Supported types:** PDFs, YouTube URLs, web URLs, Google Docs, text files, Markdown, Word docs, audio files, video files, images
343	
344	### Bulk Import with Source Waiting (Subagent Pattern)
345	**Time:** Varies by source count
346	
347	When adding multiple sources and needing to wait for processing before chat/generation:
348	
349	1. Add sources with `--json` to capture IDs:
350	   ```bash
351	   notebooklm source add "https://url1.com" --json  # → {"source_id": "abc..."}
352	   notebooklm source add "https://url2.com" --json  # → {"source_id": "def..."}
353	   ```
354	2. **Spawn a background agent** to wait for all sources:
355	   ```
356	   Task(
357	     prompt="Wait for sources {source_ids} in notebook {notebook_id} to be ready.
358	             For each: notebooklm source wait {id} -n {notebook_id} --timeout 120
359	             Report when all ready or if any fail.",
360	     subagent_type="general-purpose"
361	   )
362	   ```
363	3. Main conversation continues while agent waits
364	4. Once sources are ready, proceed with chat or generation
365	
366	**Why wait for sources?** Sources must be indexed before chat or generation. Takes 10-60 seconds per source.
367	
368	### Deep Web Research (Subagent Pattern)
369	**Time:** 2-5 minutes, runs in background
370	
371	Deep research finds and analyzes web sources on a topic:
372	
373	1. Create notebook: `notebooklm create "Research: [topic]"`
374	2. Start deep research (non-blocking):
375	   ```bash
376	   notebooklm source add-research "topic query" --mode deep --no-wait
377	   ```
378	3. **Spawn a background agent** to wait and import:
379	   ```
380	   Task(
381	     prompt="Wait for research in notebook {notebook_id} to complete and import sources.
382	             Use: notebooklm research wait -n {notebook_id} --import-all --timeout 300
383	             Report how many sources were imported.",
384	     subagent_type="general-purpose"
385	   )
386	   ```
387	4. Main conversation continues while agent waits
388	5. When agent completes, sources are imported automatically
389	
390	**Alternative (blocking):** For simple cases, omit `--no-wait`:
391	```bash
392	notebooklm source add-research "topic" --mode deep --import-all
393	# Blocks for up to 5 minutes
394	```
395	
396	**When to use each mode:**
397	- `--mode fast`: Specific topic, quick overview needed (5-10 sources, seconds)
398	- `--mode deep`: Broad topic, comprehensive analysis needed (20+ sources, 2-5 min)
399	
400	**Research sources:**
401	- `--from web`: Search the web (default)
402	- `--from drive`: Search Google Drive
403	
404	## Output Style
405	
406	**Progress updates:** Brief status for each step
407	- "Creating notebook 'Research: AI'..."
408	- "Adding source: https://example.com..."
409	- "Starting audio generation... (task ID: abc123)"
410	
411	**Fire-and-forget for long operations:**
412	- Start generation, return artifact ID immediately
413	- Do NOT poll or wait in main conversation - generation takes 5-45 minutes (see timing table)
414	- User checks status manually, OR use subagent with `artifact wait`
415	
416	**JSON output:** Use `--json` flag for machine-readable output:
417	```bash
418	notebooklm list --json
419	notebooklm auth check --json
420	notebooklm source list --json
421	notebooklm artifact list --json
422	```
423	
424	**JSON schemas (key fields):**
425	
426	`notebooklm list --json`:
427	```json
428	{"notebooks": [{"id": "...", "title": "...", "created_at": "..."}]}
429	```
430	
431	`notebooklm auth check --json`:
432	```json
433	{"checks": {"storage_exists": true, "json_valid": true, "cookies_present": true, "sid_cookie": true, "token_fetch": true}, "details": {"storage_path": "...", "auth_source": "file", "cookies_found": ["SID", "HSID", "..."], "cookie_domains": [".google.com"]}}
434	```
435	
436	`notebooklm source list --json`:
437	```json
438	{"sources": [{"id": "...", "title": "...", "status": "ready|processing|error"}]}
439	```
440	
441	`notebooklm artifact list --json`:
442	```json
443	{"artifacts": [{"id": "...", "title": "...", "type": "Audio Overview", "status": "in_progress|pending|completed|unknown"}]}
444	```
445	
446	**Status values:**
447	- Sources: `processing` → `ready` (or `error`)
448	- Artifacts: `pending` or `in_progress` → `completed` (or `unknown`)

450	## Error Handling
451	
452	**On failure, offer the user a choice:**
453	1. Retry the operation
454	2. Skip and continue with something else
455	3. Investigate the error
456	
457	**Error decision tree:**
458	
459	| Error | Cause | Action |
460	|-------|-------|--------|
461	| Auth/cookie error | Session expired | Run `notebooklm auth check` then `notebooklm login` |
462	| "No notebook context" | Context not set | Use `-n <id>` or `--notebook <id>` flag (parallel), or `notebooklm use <id>` (single-agent) |
463	| "No result found for RPC ID" | Rate limiting | Wait 5-10 min, retry |
464	| `GENERATION_FAILED` | Google rate limit | Wait and retry later |
465	| Download fails | Generation incomplete | Check `artifact list` for status |
466	| Invalid notebook/source ID | Wrong ID | Run `notebooklm list` to verify |
467	| RPC protocol error | Google changed APIs | May need CLI update |
468	
469	## Exit Codes
470	
471	All commands use consistent exit codes:
472	
473	| Code | Meaning | Action |
474	|------|---------|--------|
475	| 0 | Success | Continue |
476	| 1 | Error (not found, processing failed) | Check stderr, see Error Handling |
477	| 2 | Timeout (wait commands only) | Extend timeout or check status manually |
478	
479	**Examples:**
480	- `source wait` returns 1 if source not found or processing failed
481	- `artifact wait` returns 2 if timeout reached before completion
482	- `generate` returns 1 if rate limited (check stderr for details)
483	
484	## Known Limitations
485	
486	**Rate limiting:** Audio, video, quiz, flashcards, infographic, and slide deck generation may fail due to Google's rate limits. This is an API limitation, not a bug.
487	
488	**Reliable operations:** These always work:
489	- Notebooks (list, create, delete, rename)
490	- Sources (add, list, delete)
491	- Chat/queries
492	- Mind-map, study-guide, report, data-table generation
493	
494	**Unreliable operations:** These may fail with rate limiting:
495	- Audio (podcast) generation
496	- Video generation
497	- Quiz and flashcard generation
498	- Infographic and slide deck generation
499	
500	**Workaround:** If generation fails:
501	1. Check status: `notebooklm artifact list`
502	2. Retry after 5-10 minutes
503	3. Use the NotebookLM web UI as fallback
504	
505	**Processing times vary significantly.** Use the subagent pattern for long operations:
506	
507	| Operation | Typical time | Suggested timeout |
508	|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
509	| Source processing | 30s - 10 min | 600s |
510	| Research (fast) | 30s - 2 min | 180s |
511	| Research (deep) | 15 - 30+ min | 1800s |
512	| Notes | instant | n/a |
513	| Mind-map | instant (sync) | n/a |
514	| Quiz, flashcards | 5 - 15 min | 900s |
515	| Report, data-table | 5 - 15 min | 900s |
516	| Audio generation | 10 - 20 min | 1200s |
517	| Video generation | 15 - 45 min | 2700s |
518	
519	**Polling intervals:** When checking status manually, poll every 15-30 seconds to avoid excessive API calls.
520	
521	## Language Configuration
522	
523	Language setting controls the output language for generated artifacts (audio, video, etc.).
524	
525	**Important:** Language is a **GLOBAL** setting that affects all notebooks in your account.
526	
527	```bash
528	# List all 80+ supported languages with native names
529	notebooklm language list
530	
531	# Show current language setting
532	notebooklm language get
533	
534	# Set language for artifact generation
535	notebooklm language set zh_Hans  # Simplified Chinese
536	notebooklm language set ja       # Japanese
537	notebooklm language set en       # English (default)
538	```
539	
540	**Common language codes:**
541	| Code | Language |
542	|------|----------|
543	| `en` | English |
544	| `zh_Hans` | 中文（简体） - Simplified Chinese |
545	| `zh_Hant` | 中文（繁體） - Traditional Chinese |
546	| `ja` | 日本語 - Japanese |
547	| `ko` | 한국어 - Korean |
548	| `es` | Español - Spanish |
549	| `fr` | Français - French |
550	| `de` | Deutsch - German |
551	| `pt_BR` | Português (Brasil) |
552	
553	**Override per command:** Use `--language` flag on generate commands:
554	```bash
555	notebooklm generate audio --language ja   # Japanese podcast
556	notebooklm generate video --language zh_Hans  # Chinese video
557	```
558	
559	**Offline mode:** Use `--local` flag to skip server sync:
560	```bash
561	notebooklm language set zh_Hans --local  # Save locally only
562	notebooklm language get --local  # Read local config only
563	```
564	
565	## Troubleshooting
566	
567	```bash
568	notebooklm --help              # Main commands
569	notebooklm auth check          # Diagnose auth issues
570	notebooklm auth check --test   # Full auth validation with network test
571	notebooklm notebook --help     # Notebook management
572	notebooklm source --help       # Source management
573	notebooklm research --help     # Research status/wait
574	notebooklm generate --help     # Content generation
575	notebooklm artifact --help     # Artifact management
576	notebooklm download --help     # Download content
577	notebooklm language --help     # Language settings
578	```
579	
580	**Diagnose auth:** `notebooklm auth check` - shows cookie domains, storage path, validation status
581	**Re-authenticate:** `notebooklm login`
582	**Check version:** `notebooklm --version`
583	**Refresh a CLI-managed install:** `notebooklm skill install`
584

Based on the official Claude Code documentation, here's what I found about skills in the desktop app:

## How Skills Work in Desktop vs CLI

**Both the Claude desktop app and CLI load skills from the same locations:**

1. **Personal skills**: `~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`
2. **Project skills**: `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` 
3. **Plugin skills**: Distributed through plugins

**There is no difference in skill loading between CLI and desktop** — they use the same skill discovery mechanism. The desktop app should automatically discover and load skills from `~/.claude/skills/` just like the CLI does.

## Why Your Skill Might Not Be Showing Up

If you installed a skill to `~/.claude/skills/notebooklm/SKILL.md` but it's not appearing in the desktop app after a restart, check these issues:

1. **File permissions**: Ensure the file is readable by your user
2. **Correct directory structure**: The skill must be in a subdirectory with `SKILL.md` as the filename (not `skill.md` or other variations)
3. **Valid YAML frontmatter**: If the `SKILL.md` is malformed, it won't load. Check for:
   - Proper `---` delimiters at top and bottom
   - Valid YAML syntax in the frontmatter
   - A `description` field (recommended) so the skill shows up properly

4. **Desktop app cache**: Try fully quitting and restarting the desktop app
5. **Check the skill was discovered**: In a desktop session, ask Claude "What skills are available?" or type `/` to see if the skill appears in the autocomplete menu

## Testing

To verify the skill is discoverable:
- In the desktop app, type `/` in the prompt box — you should see `notebooklm` in the list
- Or ask Claude: "Show me what skills I have available"

The documentation emphasizes that skills at `~/.claude/skills/` are **personal-level skills** that apply across all your projects (both CLI and desktop), so if the file structure and YAML are correct, it should work identically in both interfaces.

If you've verified the structure is correct and it's still not showing, check the desktop app's logs or try [restarting it completely](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting.md) to clear any cached data.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Remotion Claude Code skill installation and Cowork:

## Remotion Agent Skills Overview

Remotion maintains a list of Agent Skills that define best practices for working in Remotion projects, and these skills are useful for AI agents like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.

## Installation

The actual install is almost too simple — according to the official Remotion documentation, you run one line. The command downloads skill files to .claude/skills in your project (or ~/.claude/skills for global Claude Code access), and you should see SKILL.md plus folders like rules/animations.md, rules/audio.md, etc.

## Using Skills in Cowork

In Cowork, click Customize in the left sidebar, then click the button to open the directory and click the Skills tab. On Team and Enterprise plans, you can share skills you've created with specific colleagues or with your entire organization, and skill sharing works in both chat and Cowork.

## What Remotion Skills Do

Remotion Agent Skills are the "instruction manual" you install into Claude Code so it understands how to write code correctly — without these skills, Claude struggles with Remotion's patterns, but with the skills installed, Claude gains a mental model of frames, scenes, and component logic.

what kind of videos can you create with remotion

> AGENT

Remotion is a framework for creating videos **programmatically with React and code**. It's great for:

**Data & Business**
- Data visualizations and animated charts
- Video reports and dashboards
- Product demos and walkthroughs

**Social Media**
- Reels/Shorts with animated text and graphics
- Meme videos
- Quote cards with motion

**Developer / Tech**
- Code walkthroughs with syntax highlighting
- GitHub contribution graphs
- Animated diagrams and architecture charts

**Marketing**
- Personalized video ads at scale (generate 1000s of variations)
- Explainer videos
- Promo clips with dynamic data

**Educational**
- Animated tutorials
- Slide-deck style videos
- Math/science visualizations

**Creative**
- Motion graphics
- Generative art videos
- Music visualizers

The key advantage of Remotion is **programmability** — if you can describe it in code (loop through data, pull from an API, generate variations), you can make a video of it. It's not a general-purpose video editor like Premiere — it shines when you need **repeatable, data-driven, or templated** video content.

Want to try making something specific?

> DEVELOPER

first define generatve art

> AGENT

**Generative art** is art created by a system — usually code — that runs autonomously to produce the output. Instead of drawing every frame by hand, you define **rules and parameters**, and the algorithm generates the visual result, often with an element of randomness or mathematical complexity.

Key traits:
- **Rule-based** — you set the logic, not every pixel
- **Often unpredictable** — small changes in parameters produce wildly different results
- **Reproducible** — same seed = same output (or not, if intentionally random)
- **Infinite variation** — the system can generate endless unique pieces

Classic examples:
- Conway's Game of Life (cells living/dying by rules)
- Fractals like the Mandelbrot set
- Flow fields driven by Perlin noise
- Neural style transfer

In the context of **video**, generative art means the visuals are computed frame-by-frame by code — no keyframing, no manual animation. Remotion is a perfect fit because it renders each frame as a React component, so you can feed it math, noise functions, physics simulations, or any algorithm and it becomes a video.

Want to pick a style and make one?

> DEVELOPER

can remotion create photo realistic videos

> AGENT

No. Remotion renders **web technologies** (React, HTML, CSS, Canvas, WebGL) — it's essentially a headless browser that records each frame. That means:

**What it can do well:**
- Sharp 2D graphics and animations
- WebGL shaders (can look stunning, but stylized not realistic)
- SVG and vector art
- Text and UI animations
- Compositing with real video/image files

**What it cannot do:**
- 3D ray tracing / path tracing
- Realistic lighting, shadows, reflections
- Physically-based rendering (PBR)
- Anything that requires a 3D render engine like Blender, Unreal, or Cinema 4D

**The honest answer:** If you want photorealistic video, Remotion is the wrong tool. You'd want something like:
- **Blender** (free, powerful 3D renderer)
- **Unreal Engine** (real-time photorealistic)
- **AI video generators** (Sora, Runway, Kling) for AI-generated realism

Remotion's sweet spot is **graphic design in motion** — think motion graphics, data viz, UI animations, and stylized generative art. It can look beautiful and polished, just not photorealistic.

  "content": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig } from \"remotion\";\nimport { useMemo, useRef } from \"react\";\n\n// Simple deterministic noise (no external deps)\nfunction fade(t: number) { return t * t * t * (t * (t * 6 - 15) + 10); }\nfunction lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number) { return a + t * (b - a); }\nfunction grad(hash: number, x: number, y: number) {\n  const h = hash & 3;\n  const u = h < 2 ? x : y;\n  const v = h < 2 ? y : x;\n  return ((h & 1) ? -u : u) + ((h & 2) ? -v : v);\n}\nconst P = Array.from({ length: 256 }, (_, i) => i).sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5);\nconst perm = [...P, ...P];\nfunction noise(x: number, y: number) {\n  const xi = Math.floor(x) & 255;\n  const yi = Math.floor(y) & 255;\n  const xf = x - Math.floor(x);\n  const yf = y - Math.floor(y);\n  const u = fade(xf);\n  const v = fade(yf);\n  const aa = perm[perm[xi] + yi];\n  const ab = perm[perm[xi] + yi + 1];\n  const ba = perm[perm[xi + 1] + yi];\n  const bb = perm[perm[xi + 1] + yi + 1];\n  return lerp(\n    lerp(grad(aa, xf, yf), grad(ba, xf - 1, yf), u),\n    lerp(grad(ab, xf, yf - 1), grad(bb, xf - 1, yf - 1), u),\n    v\n  );\n}\n\nconst NUM_PARTICLES = 600;\nconst SEED = 42;\n\nfunction seededRandom(seed: number) {\n  let s = seed;\n  return () => {\n    s = (s * 16807 + 0) % 2147483647;\n    return (s - 1) / 2147483646;\n  };\n}\n\ninterface Particle {\n  x: number;\n  y: number;\n  hue: number;\n  speed: number;\n  size: number;\n}\n\nfunction advanceParticles(\n  particles: Particle[],\n  steps: number,\n  W: number,\n  H: number,\n  time: number\n): { pts: Particle[]; trails: Array<{ x: number; y: number; hue: number; alpha: number; size: number }[]> } {\n  const pts = particles.map((p) => ({ ...p }));\n  const trails: Array<{ x: number; y: number; hue: number; alpha: number; size: number }[]> =\n    pts.map((p) => [{ x: p.x, y: p.y, hue: p.hue, alpha: 1, size: p.size }]);\n\n  for (let s = 0; s < steps; s++) {\n    for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {\n      const p = pts[i];\n      const angle = noise(p.x / 300 + time * 0.3, p.y / 300 + time * 0.3) * Math.PI * 4;\n      p.x += Math.cos(angle) * p.speed;\n      p.y += Math.sin(angle) * p.speed;\n      if (p.x < 0) p.x += W;\n      if (p.x > W) p.x -= W;\n      if (p.y < 0) p.y += H;\n      if (p.y > H) p.y -= H;\n      const alpha = 1 - s / steps;\n      trails[i].push({ x: p.x, y: p.y, hue: p.hue, alpha, size: p.size });\n    }\n  }\n  return { pts, trails };\n}\n\nexport const MyComposition: React.FC = () => {\n  const frame = useCurrentFrame();\n  const { width, height, fps, durationInFrames } = useVideoConfig();\n\n  const initialParticles = useMemo<Particle[]>(() => {\n    const rng = seededRandom(SEED);\n    return Array.from({ length: NUM_PARTICLES }, () => ({\n      x: rng() * width,\n      y: rng() * height,\n      hue: rng() * 360,\n      speed: 1.5 + rng() * 2.5,\n      size: 1 + rng() * 2,\n    }));\n  }, [width, height]);\n\n  const time = frame / fps;\n  const TRAIL = 20;\n\n  const { trails } = useMemo(\n    () => advanceParticles(initialParticles, frame + TRAIL, width, height, time),\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n    [frame]\n  );\n\n  const progress = frame / durationInFrames;\n  const bgLightness = 5 + progress * 3;\n\n  return (\n    <div\n      style={{\n        width,\n        height,\n        background: `hsl(240,20%,${bgLightness}%)`,\n        overflow: \"hidden\",\n        position: \"relative\",\n      }}\n    >\n      <svg width={width} height={height} style={{ position: \"absolute\", inset: 0 }}>\n        {trails.map((trail, i) => {\n          if (trail.length < 2) return null;\n          const points = trail\n            .slice(-TRAIL)\n            .map((pt) => `${pt.x.toFixed(1)},${pt.y.toFixed(1)}`)\n            .join(\" \");\n          const tip = trail[trail.length - 1];\n          return (\n            <g key={i}>\n              <polyline\n                points={points}\n                fill=\"none\"\n                stroke={`hsla(${tip.hue},90%,65%,0.18)`}\n                strokeWidth={tip.size * 2}\n                strokeLinecap=\"round\"\n                strokeLinejoin=\"round\"\n              />\n              <circle\n                cx={tip.x}\n                cy={tip.y}\n                r={tip.size}\n                fill={`hsla(${tip.hue},100%,80%,0.9)`}\n              />\n            </g>\n          );\n        })}\n      </svg>\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n"
}

Math.floor(x);\n  const yf = y - Math.floor(y);\n  const u = fade(xf);\n  const v = fade(yf);\n  const aa = perm[perm[xi] + yi];\n  const ab = perm[perm[xi] + yi + 1];\n  const ba = perm[perm[xi + 1] + yi];\n  const bb = perm[perm[xi + 1] + yi + 1];\n  return lerp(\n    lerp(grad(aa, xf, yf), grad(ba, xf - 1, yf), u),\n    lerp(grad(ab, xf, yf - 1), grad(bb, xf - 1, yf - 1), u),\n    v\n  );\n}\n\nconst NUM_PARTICLES = 500;\nconst TRAIL_LENGTH = 25;\n\nfunction seededRandom(seed: number) {\n  let s = seed;\n  return () => {\n    s = (s * 16807) % 2147483647;\n    return (s - }

(\n          <circle key={i} cx={CX} cy={CY} r={radius}\n            fill=\"none\" stroke={`rgba(90,255,140,${op})`}\n            strokeWidth={Math.max(0.3, 2 - rp * 2)} />\n        ) : null;\n      })}\n\n      {/* Signal lines */}\n      {postP > 0 && Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => {\n        const angle = (i / 10) * Math.PI * 2 + 0.3;\n        const len = postP * 320;\n        const op = postP * 0.55;\n        return (\n          <line key={i}\n            x1={CX + Math.cos(angle) * 215} y1={CY + Math.sin(angle) * 215}\n            x2={CX + Math.cos(angle) * (215 + len)} y2={CY + Math.sin(angle) * (215 + len)}\n            stroke={`rgba(90,255,140,${op})`} strokeWidth={1}\n            strokeDasharray={`${10 * postP},8`} />\n        );\n      })}\n\n      {/* Traveling exosome */}\n      {p < CONN + 0.04 && (\n        <g filter=\"url(#s3exoGlow)\" opacity={Math.min(1, (1 - exP) * 8)}>\n          <circle cx={exCX} cy={exCY} r={24} fill=\"rgba(90,175,255,0.2)\" />\n          <circle cx={exCX} cy={exCY} r={14} fill=\"#4a9eff\" />\n          <circle cx={exCX - 5} cy={exCY - 5} r={5} fill=\"rgba(210,235,255,0.9)\" />\n        </g>\n      )}\n\n      <text x={72} y={68} fill=\"rgba(90,220,140,0.75)\" fontSize={26}\n        fontFamily=\"Georgia,serif\" letterSpacing={5}>\n        CELLULAR REPAIR ACTIVATION\n      </text>\n    </g>\n  );\n}\n\n// ── Scene 4 – Results: Organized Collagen ─────────────────────────────────────\nfunction Scene4({ f }: { f: number }) {\n  const p = prog(f, SC.results);\n\n  return (\n    <g>\n      <defs>\n        <linearGradient id=\"s4bg\" x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"0\" y2=\"1\"\n          gradientUnits=\"userSpaceOnUse\" y2={H}>\n          <stop offset=\"0%\" stopColor=\"rgba(160,85,35,0.35)\" />\n          <stop offset=\"100%\" stopColor=\"rgba(30,10,3,0.35)\" />\n        </linearGradient>\n      </defs>\n      <rect x={0} y={0} width={W} height={H} fill=\"url(#s4bg)\" />\n\n      {/* Organized collagen lines drawing in left→right */}\n      {NEW_COLLAGEN.map((ln, i) => {\n        const lineStart = (i / NEW_COLLAGEN.length) * 0.45;\n        const lp = clamp01((p - lineStart) / 0.55);\n        if (lp <= 0) return null;\n\n        const STEPS = 160;\n        const drawTo = Math.floor(lp * STEPS);\n        const pts = Array.from({ length: drawTo + 1 }, (_, j) => {\n          const x = (j / STEPS) * W;\n          const y = ln.yBase + Math.sin(x * ln.freq + ln.phase) * ln.amp;\n          return `${x.toFixed(1)},${y.toFixed(1)}`;\n        });\n        if (pts.length < 2) return null;\n\n        return (\n          <polyline key={i} points={pts.join(\" \")} fill=\"none\"\n            stroke={`hsla(${ln.hue},58%,${ln.light}%,${0.45 + lp * 0.45})`}\n            strokeWidth={ln.sw} strokeLinecap=\"round\" />\n        );\n      })}\n\n      {/* Warm glow as lines fill in */}\n      {p > 0.65 && (\n        <rect x={0} y={0} width={W} height={H}\n          fill={`rgba(210,140,60,${(p - 0.65) * 0.09})`} />\n      )}\n\n      {/* BEFORE / AFTER divider during mid-phase */}\n      {p > 0.1 && p < 0.88 && (\n        <>\n          <line x1={p * W * 1.1} y1={0} x2={p * W * 1.1} y2={H}\n            stroke=\"rgba(230,180,100,0.35)\" strokeWidth={2} />\n          <text x={60} y={H - 90} fill=\"rgba(140,90,50,0.55)\" fontSize={22}\n            fontFamily=\"Georgia,serif\" letterSpacing={3}>BEFORE</text>\n          <text x={Math.min(p * W * 1.1 + 20, W - 200)} y={H - 90}\n            fill=\"rgba(230,180,100,0.8)\" fontSize={22}\n            fontFamily=\"Georgia,serif\" letterSpacing={3}>AFTER</text>\n        </>\n      )}\n\n      <text x={72} y={68} fill=\"rgba(230,175,100,0.75)\" fontSize={26}\n        fontFamily=\"Georgia,serif\" letterSpacing={5}>\n        STRUCTURAL RENEWAL\n      </text>\n    </g>\n  );\n}\n\n// ── Scene 5 – Usage: Brand Finish ────────────────────────────────────────────\nfunction Scene5({ f }: { f: number }) {\n  const p = prog(f, SC.usage);\n  const titleOp = clamp01(p * 3.5);\n  const lineOp  = clamp01((p - 0.12) * 3.5);\n  const subOp   = clamp01((p - 0.28) * 3.5);\n\n  return (\n    <g>\n      <defs>\n        <radialGradient id=\"s5bg\" cx=\"50%\" cy=\"44%\" r=\"58%\"\n          gradientUnits=\"userSpaceOnUse\" fx={W / 2} fy={H * 0.44}>\n          <stop offset=\"0%\" stopColor=\"rgba(130,60,18,0.65)\" />\n          <stop offset=\"55%\" stopColor=\"rgba(40,14,4,0.45)\" />\n          <stop offset=\"100%\" stopColor=\"rgba(4,2,1,0)\" />\n        </radialGradient>\n      </defs>\n      <rect x={0} y={0} width={W} height={H} fill=\"url(#s5bg)\" />\n\n      {/* Decorative rings */}\n      {[280, 430, 600, 780].map((r, i) => (\n        <circle key={i} cx={W / 2} cy={H * 0.41} r={r}\n          fill=\"none\" stroke={`rgba(210,155,75,${lineOp * (0.1 - i * 0.02)})`}\n          strokeWidth={1} />\n      ))}\n\n      {/* Brand name */}\n      <text x={W / 2} y={H * 0.38} textAnchor=\"middle\"\n        fill={`rgba(245,228,200,${titleOp})`}\n        fontSize={100} fontFamily=\"Georgia,'Times New Roman',serif\"\n        letterSpacing={16} fontWeight={400}>\n        EXOSOME SERUMS\n      </text>\n\n      {/* Decorative line */}\n      <line x1={(W - 560 * lineOp) / 2} y1={H * 0.455}\n        x2={(W + 560 * lineOp) / 2} y2={H * 0.455}\n        stroke={`rgba(210,155,75,${lineOp * 0.9})`} strokeWidth={1} />\n\n      {/* Tagline */}\n      <text x={W / 2} y={H * 0.535} textAnchor=\"middle\"\n        fill={`rgba(210,175,130,${subOp})`}\n        fontSize={34} fontFamily=\"Georgia,'Times New Roman',serif\"\n        letterSpacing={10} fontWeight={300}>\n        RESTORE · REBUILD · RENEW\n      </text>\n    </g>\n  );\n}\n\n// ── Captions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nconst CAPTIONS: { sc: Scene; text: string }[] = [\n  { sc: SC.problem,   text: \"As skin ages, its internal support system fails. Collagen fibers become thin and disorganized, while essential repair cells lose their energy and slow down.\" },\n  { sc: SC.treatment, text: \"To address this, an advanced treatment is applied. It delivers millions of nutrient-packed messengers deep below the surface to target aging cells directly.\" },\n  { sc: SC.cellular,  text: \"When an exosome connects with a cell, it triggers an instant repair signal. This jumpstarts the skin's natural ability to rebuild itself from the inside out.\" },\n  { sc: SC.results,   text: \"The transformation is visible. After treatment, the skin is reinforced with a strong, organized foundation for a smoother, firmer surface.\" },\n  { sc: SC.usage,     text: \"With just a few professional sessions, Exosome Serums helps the skin regain its strength and look its absolute best.\" },\n];\n\n// ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nexport const MyComposition: React.FC = () => {\n  const f = useCurrentFrame();\n\n  return (\n    <div style={{ width: W, height: H, background: \"#080405\", position: \"relative\", overflow: \"hidden\" }}>\n      <svg width={W} height={H} style={{ position: \"absolute\", inset: 0 }}>\n        {sceneOp(f, SC.problem) > 0 && (\n          <g opacity={sceneOp(f, SC.problem)}><Scene1 f={f} /></g>\n        )}\n        {sceneOp(f, SC.treatment) > 0 && (\n          <g opacity={sceneOp(f, SC.treatment)}><Scene2 f={f} /></g>\n        )}\n        {sceneOp(f, SC.cellular) > 0 && (\n          <g opacity={sceneOp(f, SC.cellular)}><Scene3 f={f} /></g>\n        )}\n        {sceneOp(f, SC.results) > 0 && (\n          <g opacity={sceneOp(f, SC.results)}><Scene4 f={f} /></g>\n        )}\n        {sceneOp(f, SC.usage) > 0 && (\n          <g opacity={sceneOp(f, SC.usage)}><Scene5 f={f} /></g>\n        )}\n      </svg>\n\n      {/* Captions */}\n      {CAPTIONS.map(({ sc, text }, i) => {\n        const op = sceneOp(f, sc);\n        return op > 0 ? <Caption key={i} text={text} opacity={op} /> : null;\n      })}\n\n      {/* Vignette */}\n      <div style={{\n        position: \"absolute\", inset: 0, pointerEvents: \"none\",\n        background: \"radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 45%, rgba(0,0,0,0.72) 100%)\",\n      }} />\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n"
}

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Firecrawl MCP server and how to install it with Claude:

## Installation Methods

To install Firecrawl for Claude Desktop automatically via Smithery: `npx -y @smithery/cli install @mendableai/mcp-server-firecrawl --client claude`

## Using Claude Code CLI

You can add the Firecrawl MCP server using the Claude Code CLI either via a remote hosted URL or by running it locally via npx: `claude mcp add firecrawl --url https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/your-api-key/v2/mcp` or `claude mcp add firecrawl -e FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=your-api-key -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp`

## Direct NPX Installation

You can run one command (`npx -y firecrawl-mcp`) to install the official server.

## Global NPM Installation

You can also install it globally with `npm install -g firecrawl-mcp`

## Configuration

After installation, you need to add configuration to your settings file with your Firecrawl API key in the environment variables. You can get your API key from https://firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys
